1956, November 9
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.F.M. Cap.
PAX ET BONUM ST. FELIX FRIARY CAPUCHIN FRANCISCAN FATHERS HUNTINGTON, INDIANA
Nov. 9th 1956 Following refers to the Egan case of (Pt. Euron) -- Smiths Creek Case Jan. 10º 1925
"How much is it going to cost you?", I asked. "Well I suppose it will be twenty-five dollars.", he answered, "Listen. ", I said. "You get after the holy souls in Purgatory, especially your relatives, etc, who may be there waiting for prayers. Promise them a % of that 25.00 as an enrollment if you be able to forget that appointment." "Gee!" "I'll give them half of it - I'll go them fifty-fifty.' He drove
He drove back every week after that for quite a time, seemingly never thinking any more of doctoring. If I remember rightly, it was February 29t that he quite a number of his children along with your Mother, as in fact he nearly always did, and quite smilingly proposed about as follows: "Father: I want to give the Poor Souls a good half of that X-ray which was never taken. Enroll them for $14.00.
It was a few years later that I went to Smith's Creek on a visit and your Father cams in about as was about to leave and took me to see his home, etc. And just incidently, it was on that occasion that I remen- ber seeing little Dorothy as a possible candidate for a convent or a missionary.
Now, if you send me the little victim of poleo's name, I shall be glad to enroll her in the Ser. Mass- Association and we'll hope and pray for a favorable surprise. In the mean time, however, induec as many as possible to help sorm Heaven by frequent and even dzily Communion. And do not forget the poor suffering souls in Purgatory, -- especially benefactors, relatives and the "most abandoned".
Sincerely Yours in Christ, Fr. Solanus, O.F.M. Cap.
Note: Included is a note to Friary Secretary in Fr. Solanus' hand, "Write it up as it ought to -- if you can.
